key_concepts: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity
Momentum is a vector quantity with units kg m/s
Greater mass or velocity increases momentum and collision impact
A force is required to change an object's momentum
Impulse is the product of net force and time interval
The impulse-momentum theorem states that change in momentum equals impulse
Objects with greater momentum require greater force to stop
Greater momentum leads to greater stopping distance in collisions
Energy is transferred to heat, noise, or internal energy during bounces
Seatbelts, airbags, crumple zones, and sports padding reduce collision impact
